summary: Source-reviewed re-adjudication found this eLife paper supports Bim/Bcl-2-family cancer-apoptosis interaction and cell-death evidence, while DRAMP antimicrobial and exact-sequence assertions remain conflict/database-only cautions rather than accepted primary-source facts.

materials_exhausted.notes: Checked local XML/PDF text, extracted OA package/source data spreadsheets, figure captions, supplementary table parse, and linked DRAMP rows. No primary antimicrobial MIC/hemolysis assay values were present locally.

per_layer_decision_rationale.layer_1_database: Literature linkage to the paper is real, but DRAMP activity labels and exact sequence strings exceed primary-source support; all 12 linked rows remain source_conflict with locators and caution context.
per_layer_decision_rationale.layer_2_activity_toxicity: Table 1 and source spreadsheets support Bcl-XL/Bcl-2 FLIM-FRET resistance values and a contextual MCF-7 cell-death EC50; no antimicrobial MIC/hemolysis row is invented.
per_layer_decision_rationale.layer_3_mechanism: Mechanism is limited to Bim BH3/CTS binding and apoptosis-context evidence; prior generic membrane/nucleic-acid notes were removed.
per_layer_decision_rationale.worker_6_final: The open ticket is closed because the source-supported obtainable material is now represented and unsupported database claims are explicit cautions rather than unresolved rework.

caution_findings.evidence_context: DRAMP says Antimicrobial, Anticancer for 12 records, but local primary material supports Bcl-2-family interaction/cancer-cell death context and lacks antimicrobial assay values.
Construct/mutation names and values are source-located; exact full DRAMP sequence strings are not present as extractable primary text and remain database assertions.
This paper is cancer biology/apoptosis focused; curation should not export antimicrobial MIC/hemolysis claims from it.
